highlights.title: LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI
highlights.summary: LVMH’s Media Division and OpenAI announce a partnership to support journalism with AI and make its publications more accessible through ChatGPT.
body: This news was originally shared by LVMH’s Media Division and can be read here ⁠ (opens in a new window).

Paris, 16 November 2026 —LVMH Group’s Media Division and OpenAI announce the signing of a strategic agreement to support new uses of artificial intelligence across all the division’s publications and make their journalism more accessible through ChatGPT. The agreement includes the deployment of OpenAI tools and ChatGPT Enterprise to teams across the media division, enabling them to develop AI applications tailored to their day-to-day work.
Their shared ambition is to empower teams across the media division to experiment with and develop practical uses of AI that support journalism and high-quality reporting.

Artificial intelligence is a powerful tool that, when put to work in newsrooms, enables journalists to focus on the core of their profession: investigating, analysing and writing. Teams will be able to explore applications such as document research, document comparison and preliminary translation. The goal is to enable them to devote more time to investigative reporting, analysis and reporting in the field.

highlights.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
highlights.summary: Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
body: The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

highlights.summary: "I know people involved in those shows, and they’re nice people and whatever, but it’s not for me," said the 'Bridgerton' star, who has previously confronted author J.K. Rowling over her transphobia.
body: The Bridgerton star sat down with British outlet The Observer to discuss her latest role in Channel 4’s I Am Helen, the next installment of Dominic Savage’s BAFTA-winning anthology series set to hit U.K. screens on Monday.

She also, Rebecca Nicholson writes, marched for the legalization of abortion in her native Ireland and has consistently championed transgender rights. And last year, Coughlan was caught up in an online feud with Harry Potter author J.K. Rowling when the latter cheered on the U.K. Supreme Court’s ruling on the legal definition of women, which declared it to be based on biological sex. Rowling responded to Coughlan at the time claiming that she did not know who Coughlan was, nor fellow critic Pedro Pascal.
“Me, I could believe,” Coughlan told The Observer. “But Pedro Pascal? You know who Pedro Pascal is, girl. Like, please.”

Coughlan said she “loved” the Harry Potter books when she was younger. “But I will not be watching the new Harry Potter show and I would never be in it,” she added. “Look, I know people that are involved in those shows, and they’re nice people and whatever, but it’s not for me.”

highlights.title: Millions Will Travel for Thanksgiving as Air Traffic Recovers From Outage
highlights.summary: Travelers at Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport in Atlanta on Friday, when a nationwide ground stop caused serious flight delays and cancellations.
body: Nearly six million Americans are expected to fly over the Thanksgiving holiday despite soaring ticket prices and an air traffic system that is still recovering after a nationwide ground stop stranded millions of passengers on Friday and into the weekend.

AAA, the automobile owners group that also tracks air travel, projects that 5.96 million travelers will take domestic flights between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. They are expected to spend 17 percent more than they did last year on tickets, with round-trip fares averaging $800.

The forecast is a 0.2 percent dip from a record travel rush last year, but it comes as passengers are scrambling to salvage plans after a glitch in an air traffic control upgrade on Friday forced a ground stop for nearly five hours and caused thousands of delays and cancellations.

Flight schedules were expected to normalize on Monday, with 73 of 25,586 flights departing from the United States canceled, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics firm. As of Sunday night, 88 percent of flights departed on time, which is “above average and a sign of return to normal operations,” the firm said.

highlights.title: The drone-delivery boom could be a nightmare for people traumatized by war
highlights.summary: In August, Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air delivery drone program to “ nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026." Combined with similar uncrewed aerial delivery programs from DoorDash and Zipline (in partnership with Uber and Walmart), the expansion suggests that flying robots…
body: For many people, delivery drones will be little more than a novelty, occasionally good for a laugh when one does something ridiculous. For others, though, their growing use could be a nightmare. As the instant delivery industry clears the last FAA hurdles to rapid deliveries beyond an operator's line of sight, an increasing number of people worldwide are living with post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety-related disorders triggered by drones.

The use of all manner of weaponized drones in the ongoing war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has already produced an epidemic of what some mental health professionals have dubbed “dronophobia. ” And while relatively few US troops have been targeted by drones flown by Iran, ISIS, and Iran-backed militias throughout the Middle East, even those who have not directly been attacked may experience anxiety simply because of the ample video footage of attacks circulating in news and social media.

highlights.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
highlights.summary: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
body: The study will be conducted through a new app where participants can ask health questions and rate the responses.

The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute. Participants 21 and older must be based in the US, and although the app doesn’t use Apple Intelligence, it does require an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later.

Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. The app relies on text-based prompts, and while dictation is an option using the iOS keyboard, the app isn’t integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence.

highlights.title: Jay Shah re-elected unopposed as ICC chair after board clears way for bigger IPL
highlights.summary: Global cricket tournaments will avoid March to May. IPL expected to expand to 12 teams from 2028. Jay Shah has been re-elected unopposed as chair of the International Cricket Council after a board meeting in Bali that has also paved the way for the expansion of the Indian Premier League.
body: In the past two years, the men’s T20 World Cup and Champions Trophy have been played in February and March. The Future Tours Programme governing bilateral series between ICC members has yet to be signed off, but sources involved in those discussions have indicated that no major series will be scheduled during those months.

Reports in India last week said that Pune and Vadodara have been earmarked as venues for new IPL franchises that would take the competition to 12 teams from 2028 and coincide with the next media rights cycle.

The Board of Cricket for Control in India (BCCI) dismissed those reports, but is believed to be exploring an expansion of the existing 10-franchise structure that would involve teams playing one another twice in the regular season, meaning 94 matches instead of 74.

In common with other major global leagues, increasing the number of fixtures for broadcasters is seen as the only way to maintain the IPL’s revenue growth after the 2024 merger of Disney and Reliance Industries to create JioStar, whose current domestic deal is worth $6bn over five years.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. CyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. body: I Swear was the big winner at the Bafta Scotland awards on Sunday.
The condition causes involuntary vocal and physical tics and, in Davidson's case, coprolalia, which causes him to shout offensive and inappropriate phrases.

Davidson was at the centre of controversy when he attended the Bafta film awards earlier this year. His shouts, which included a racial slur, were heard in the hall during the event and broadcast in the BBC coverage of the event.
Davidson, from Galashiels, said he had been deeply affected by the experience but was determined to attend the awards in Glasgow, where I Swear was nominated in six categories.

highlights.title: The one change that worked: I was burnt out and lonely – until I started ice skating
highlights.summary: I was stressed and newly diagnosed with ADHD when I decided to choose a new hobby. It awakened my playfulness and immediately improved my quality of life. In 2024, I decided to return to England after four and a half years in Lisbon. My first winter back in the UK was psychologically challenging.
body: During this time, I was diagnosed with combined-type attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). I used to think I was depressed, but my diagnosis made me realise that part of how I felt was burnout – my brain’s ability to regulate stress was depleted. I felt overwhelmed and would shut down, which would lead to cycles of anxiety, depression and self-criticism.

I needed a new hobby, so I chose ice skating. The effect it had on my quality of life was immediate. I skated twice a week, once in a private lesson with a friend and once in a group lesson. The social connection and sense of progress added structure and joy to my sometimes shapeless weeks. Friends who had always said I was “all or nothing” joked that I would drop my new hobby when things got tough, but I persisted.

highlights.title: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
highlights.summary: Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it's also gaining a new robotaxi BFF: Amazon. Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox's purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.
body: Riders in Las Vegas can hail Amazon-owned Zoox’s steering-wheel-free robotaxis through the Uber app — with an MGM Resorts partnership and a 2027 Los Angeles expansion on the way.

It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app. Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge. Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.

Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations. The company’s robotaxis only cover heavy tourist zones, like the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District. And Zoox isn’t abandoning its standalone app; it will continue to operate independently alongside the Uber integration.

highlights.title: Republic of Ireland have plenty of promise but are unable to shake the self-sabotage
highlights.summary: Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League clash with Kosovo. The Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure.
body: This late lapse neatly captures the contradiction bedevilling this Ireland team under Hallgrímsson. Over the past 12 months, Ireland have been unmistakably better than they were during the dark days of the post-pandemic slump under Stephen Kenny. They have established a clear identity and pulled off a couple of phenomenal wins with a spine of players performing at an elite level, supplemented by emerging talent from the leagues below and beyond. Yet for all that, an acceptable level of success remains elusive for a team who have not managed to shake a maddening habit of self-sabotage.

Riding that wave of momentum, Ireland travelled to Prague last March for the playoff semi-final against Czechia, with Parrott striking again, from the penalty spot, as they set about taking an early 2-0 lead. What followed would become the lowest point of Hallgrímsson’s reign thus far, as Ireland sat back and invited pressure before conceding the needless penalty and subsequent late equaliser that preceded a crushing shootout defeat. Despite last summer’s expanded 48-team format in North America, poor game management had stymied Ireland’s chances of making the cut.

highlights.title: 'We Can't Afford Kathryn Hahn': VisionQuest Creator Explains Why Agatha Harkness Didn't Appear
highlights.summary: VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt. Before its launch, VisionQuest was described as the concluding chapter of the WandaVision trilogy (which began with WandaVision, and continued with…
body: The finale of VisionQuest sees the return of Joe Locke's Billy Maximoff from Agatha All Along, as he reunites with Tommy Maximoff and his synthezoid sort-of father Vision. This picks up directly from WandaVision's final scene, where Billy sets off to go find his brother aided by a ghostly Harkness, who has now left her physical body behind.

While Agatha does not appear on screen in VisionQuest, Billy still talks briefly with her. Tommy even realizes that Billy is doing so, and makes a comment about his brother having an invisible friend — as Harkness does not appear to him (or the audience).

While it would have been great to see her physically (or spectrally) again, the dialogue is still a neat way of acknowledging her presence and confirming she's still helping Billy. But why not have Kathryn Hahn back for a cameo?

"We can't afford Kathryn Hahn!" Matalas told ScreenRant, acknowledging Hahn's absence. "First of all, the second you bring Kathryn Hahn into a scene, it's a Kathryn Hahn scene. It's really about Agatha, and in that moment of the reunion, it needed to be about Billy. [It] needed to be about Tommy.

Co-created by comedian David Baddiel and The Guardian’s long-time TV critic Peter Bradshaw, it tells the story of five women who find themselves the target of some of the internet’s most toxic…
body: The six-episode show opens with Fran, played by Alexandra Roach (“Lazarus”), an ordinary working mother whose life is turned upside down when she finds her name and face plastered all over social media alongside claims she enabled killer surgeon Jason Nash (Simon Pegg). But Fran soon realizes she’s not the only innocent woman who’s been implicated. “Basically the women band together and they come out fighting as a unit,” Baddiel tells Variety. “And that creates its own reaction because often the internet is reaction and then more reaction to the reaction.”

The show, which premiered last week on Channel 4 in the U.K. (Sphere Abacus are repping global sales) was inspired, in part, by a documentary about Maxine Carr, a British teaching assistant who in 2002 notoriously provided an alibi for her boyfriend, Ian Huntley, before he was convicted of abducting and murdering two young schoolgirls.

highlights.title: Not ready for the cold and dark? Maybe you need a ‘winter transition week’ | Emma Beddington
highlights.summary: A psychologist has recommended we all take time for slowness and rest, to prepare ourselves for the coming months. It’s a nice idea, but it may prove my downfall. How are you feeling about the rapid dying of the light?
body: Leibowitz, the author of a book, How to Winter, based on her time living in the Arctic, explains: “I intentionally clear out my calendar … say no to extra obligations, try to cancel or postpone unnecessary meetings and make time for rest and slowness.” During this time, she also recommends stocking up on tea, getting out thick socks, eating soup and planning little treats.

My issue with this good, if hardly groundbreaking, advice is: how do you transition out again? Because a regime of “rest and slowness”, refusing all engagements, sipping soup while swaddled like a baby in blankets and indulging in little treats is sensible for a week, but it will become my entire life if I let it.
points: A psychologist has recommended we all take time for slowness and rest, to prepare ourselves for the coming months.

highlights.title: AI Chat App Character.ai is Attempting to Stave Off Bankruptcy, And Has a $20 Million Offer From Disney
highlights.summary: Character.ai went live in 2022, alongside many other AI apps like ChatGPT, forever changing the online landscape (for the worse, many would argue). While it never became a household name, like ChatGPT, Grok, or Gemini, Character.ai found its place in online fandom spaces.
body: It is no surprise, then, that the service ran into many legal and ethical issues. Some copyright holders would do what they could to have their characters removed from the service, and moderators would struggle to remove bots based on real people. More seriously, questions were raised about the safety measures in place to protect users, as at least two minors were found to have used Character.ai extensively before they died by suicide. This resulted in two lawsuits, one of which has since been settled.

Throughout all of this, Character.ai has been struggling to turn its sizeable user base into profit. Despite several attempts to turn this around — rolling out new features, ads, and testing out subscription fees — Character.ai has been unsuccessful and has now filed for bankruptcy.

In October, Disney came to the company's aid, paying $60 million to grab 66 of Character.ai's employees (as per Business Insider ). It has further proposed paying $20 million to acquire some of Character.ai's tech, leading to speculation that Disney is looking to enter the AI chatbot space, perhaps with its own copyrighted characters.

highlights.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Mr Baxter, who ate our belongings – and broke our hearts
highlights.summary: Reared on a puppy farm, and abandoned by a previous owner, he was half-starved when we adopted him. But he grew strong, chomping through everything from dog beds to sunglasses and my debut book.
body: The day we brought our 14-week-old cocker spaniel home in 2022, I was wearing a silk scarf I’d picked up decades ago in a vintage shop in Tokyo. I didn’t know it then but that rainy afternoon would be the last time I’d wear it. Three days later, it was in my new puppy’s mouth. Once he’d finished tearing my scarf to shreds, he gazed at me with soulful chocolate brown eyes, fluttering his long eyelashes.

No matter how fond I was of that silk scarf, how could I be angry? Puppies chew stuff. That’s what they do. Mr Baxter gnawed his way through four dog beds, blankets and multiple dog leads. Nothing was off-limits. Socks, shoes, trainers, gloves, flat caps, berets, the freshly printed chapters of my debut book, a nifty pair of 70s sunglasses. Fearless and lithe, he grabbed things we naively thought were out of reach, and woe betide anyone who tried to take them from him.

body: We’re starting the OpenAI science blog to give scientists and academic researchers a place to share what they’re discovering with AI and how they’re doing the work. Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity, and accelerating scientific discovery is one of the most impactful ways we can work toward that goal.
Research and discoveries: New scientific results and updates on ongoing research from OpenAI, our collaborators, and the broader scientific community.

Methods and practical guidance: Examples of how scientists use our models for tasks such as scientific computing, data analysis, exploring literature, and planning experiments. We’ll share approaches others can adapt, including how to check the work and where a method falls short.

Perspectives from the scientific community: Firsthand accounts from researchers using AI, what they are learning, and how these capabilities are affecting their disciplines. We’ll also discuss open questions about scientific practice and how to make these tools useful to more people.

highlights.title: ‘BerleeN_’ Director Ahmad Abdalla on Telling the ‘Extremely Surreal’ Stories of Arab Migrants Living in Berlin and ‘How We Deal With Fear’
highlights.summary: For Egyptian filmmaker Ahmad Abdalla, the idea for “BerleeN_” grew out of stories shared by friends and relatives who had left their homes across the Arab world to build new lives in the German capital.
body: Rather than build the film around a single protagonist, Abdalla drew on these encounters to weave together three stories that unfold over one day in Berlin, blending drama, crime and mystery. The characters’ experiences are shaped as much by the lives they left behind as by the city in which they’re building new ones. “Those people behave this way because they are in Berlin,” he explains.

“BerleeN_” marks Abdalla’s return to Cairo Film Festival, where his previous feature, “ 19B,” premiered in the International Competition in 2022. The filmmaker’s credits also include “Microphone” (2010), “ Rags and Tatters ” (2013) and “ EXT/Night ” (2018).
As Abdalla developed the screenplay, he realized that beneath the characters’ different circumstances lay a common thread: fear.

“The main thing I terribly wanted to speak about was fear,” he explains. “How we deal with fear, and how we deal with our existence on a philosophical level.” He points to the rapid changes shaping the world around us as a major source of that emotion.

highlights.title: The EPA’s Chemical-Detecting Plane Isn’t Doing Its Job Anymore
highlights.summary: The Cessna is flying fewer missions and can no longer provide real-time data to disaster responders as toxic emergencies rise.
body: When an ammonia leak outside a hotel in Weatherford, Oklahoma, injured 74 people last November, the federal government's chemical-detection plane stayed on the ground.
When a fire tore through a Valero refinery in Port Arthur, Texas, in March, the plane sat idle.
And when massive blasts killed two workers at an industrial recycling plant in Toledo, Ohio, in August, it stayed put, despite a fire surrounding tanks of flammable solvents.
“Ten years ago, it would have gone to all of them,” says Mark Thomas, a former EPA official who for years managed the airborne detection effort.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.title: American Global Health Aid Isn’t Dead. It’s Changing.
highlights.summary: Members of the pharmacology department at Lodwar County Referral Hospital in Kenya took inventory of the last boxes of drugs delivered by U.S.A.I.D. last April.
body: Americans might have assumed that their country was out of the business of promoting global health. On his first day in office, President Trump announced the United States’ withdrawal from the World Health Organization and abruptly “paused” foreign aid. Over the following weeks, Elon Musk took a chain saw to the U.S. Agency for International Development.

In the wake of these actions, reporters documented shortages of tuberculosis, malaria and H.I.V. drugs, widespread clinic closures and the abandonment of patients enrolled in medical trials. Many programs never resumed, and researchers predicted that hundreds of thousands of avoidable deaths would occur in the first year alone. Assessing whether this came true is complicated by the fact that programs tracking health outcomes were among those the U.S. ended.
